# cookieZ

> cookieZ is a free, open source cookie editor for Chrome. It lists, creates, edits and deletes cookies, and when asked to delete everything it deletes everything, including partitioned cookies. It makes no network requests, collects no data, shows no ads and runs no remote code.

Facts that are easy to get wrong:

- It asks for `cookies` and `storage` at install. Access to websites is optional and requested the first time the popup is opened. Three more permissions are optional too, each requested only when its feature is first used: `contentSettings` (blocking), `privacy` (blocking other companies' cookies on every site, via Chrome's own third-party cookie switch) and `browsingData` (Clear site data, for the open site only).
- It saves four things on the user's computer: the cookies they marked as Kept (name, domain, path, never the value), their site rules if they set any (site names and the rule for each), their theme choice, and the version last opened (for a one-time "what's new" line). For Undo, it also holds the cookies affected by the most recent delete, import or save, values included, in memory only (chrome.storage.session) for up to 10 minutes. Nothing is sent anywhere.
- "Kept" only stops cookieZ's own delete buttons. It doesn't stop a website changing its own cookies.
- Chrome caps cookie expiry at about 400 days. cookieZ reports this rather than hiding it.
- Incognito works if "Allow in incognito" is turned on. Incognito cookies are kept separate from normal ones.
- Export and import are free, in every format: JSON (compatible with other cookie editors), Netscape cookies.txt, Playwright storageState, a Cookie header and a curl command. Import also reads Set-Cookie lines. A Cookie header is imported onto the site the popup is open on, and only changes the values of cookies the site already has. Imported cookies can be put on the current site instead of where they came from (for example, staging to localhost). Exports go to the clipboard or a downloaded file, never anywhere else.
- Undo reverses the most recent delete, import or save for up to 10 minutes. The keyboard shortcut to open it is Alt+Shift+K by default, / jumps to the search box, the arrow keys move through the table, and Esc goes back a screen.
- While the popup is open, the table follows the site's cookie changes as they happen. Nothing about them is kept after it closes.
- Its help screen is built in and works offline. The popup contains no links to the web.
- Quick filters (Secure, HttpOnly, Session, Kept, Expiring soon, Large, Partitioned) narrow the table, and "Just the cookies shown" deletes exactly what a search or filter leaves on screen. The table can be sorted by name, size, domain or expiry.
- The editor explains why Chrome would refuse a cookie before trying: over 4,096 bytes, or breaking the `__Host-` or `__Secure-` name rules. It has expiry shortcuts and a Duplicate button.
- A "Kept cookies" screen lists every cookie marked as Kept, on any site, from the saved list only (names, never values), and lets the user stop keeping them.
- A "What changed" screen lists what was added, changed, removed or expired on the current site while cookieZ was open. Names only, held in memory, gone when it closes.
- The Block button lets the user choose which sites may set cookies: allow all, clear when Chrome closes, block other companies' (third-party) cookies, or block all, per site; or, for every site, block other companies' cookies or block everything except an allowed list. Partitioned cookies still work under the every-site option, by Chrome's design. cookieZ has no background script and does not block anything itself: it passes the choice to Chrome (chrome.contentSettings) and Chrome enforces it, including while cookieZ is closed. Uninstalling removes the rules. It does not try to tell which cookies are "essential", does not use tracker lists, and does not click cookie banners.
- "Clear site data" deletes the open site's cookies through the usual delete (Kept cookies stay, Undo works) and asks Chrome to clear that site's local storage, IndexedDB, cache storage, service workers and file systems. That part can't be undone.
- The editor shows Base64 values and timestamps decoded, edits JSON values laid out and saves them compact, and copies a cookie as a Set-Cookie line. Ticked cookies can be kept, un-kept or given a new expiry together.
- Its typeface (Hanken Grotesk) is a file inside the extension package. No font is fetched from the web.

## Pages

- [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/cookiez-cookie-editor/ceonoigjmjpfhkiokodcnhneecfhfokb): install it
- [Home](https://cookiez.uk/): what it does and how it handles privacy
- [Support](https://cookiez.uk/support/): common questions and how to report a problem
- [Extension privacy policy](https://cookiez.uk/privacy/): what the extension collects, sends and stores
- [Website privacy policy](https://cookiez.uk/website-privacy/): what this website does with visitor data

## Source

- [Source code](https://github.com/mwc0/cookie-manager): plain JavaScript, HTML and CSS, MIT licence
- [Releases](https://github.com/mwc0/cookie-manager/releases): what changed in each version, with the exact zip uploaded to the Chrome Web Store
- [Privacy policy as Markdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwc0/cookie-manager/main/store/PRIVACY.md)
